verdict.reason: Cerro is worth a quick check for after work (18:00 start), but it is not a guaranteed session.  Treat it as a check-first call rather than a sure thing.  Wind is the main thing to watch.  The tide and timing are lining up well for this spot.

conversationalSummary.text: TODAY after work (around 18:00) at Cerro could be the best available bet, but the wind angle is pretty poor and it may end up choppy. Before I leave, I’d check the Surfline cams and the MEO Beachcam for Cerro—if they don’t look much cleaner than expected, I’d rather skip. The tide’s rising with a bit of push, which can help on these exposed-enough beachbreak windows, so I’m only going to bother if the cams line up.

best.explanation: Cerro looks like a solid window for Worth checking, Medium confidence: 1.2-1.5 m, 270 kJ, 10 s period, consistent 66/100, and wind is the main risk.  A sheltered beachbreak with gentle lefts and rights, somewhat similar to Cantinho but less consistent; this is best for manageable bodyboard waves when north-northwest swell reaches the bay with clean southerly wind; 10-13s at mid tide works well on exposed beaches.  Watch: wind angle is poor for this spot.
